proof.text: Identify $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ by clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], applied with auxiliary commutative coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$; this clause concerns only the sites and their coverings. Apply clause (1) of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], again with auxiliary ring $\mathbf Z$, to sets, abelian sheaves and rings. For an object $W\to U$, its initial indexing pair $(W\to T,(\mathrm{str},\mathrm{id}_W):W\to U\times_TW)$ gives the natural identification $j^{-1}N(W)=N(W\to T)$. Only the ring-independent inverse-image clause is used, not that node's commutative module-pullback clause. These identifications hold on the compatible skeletons via the stated site equivalence.

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; localization restriction in Section 00XZ; proetale.tex Tag 09A5

proof.text: Let $P_S(V)=\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|V|),A)$ be the ring-valued presheaf defining $A_S$ in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Under the site identification, $P_T|_U=P_U$, including multiplication and restriction maps. Apply [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification] with values in rings: $A_T|_U=(P_T^\#)|_U\cong(P_T|_U)^\#=A_U$, preserving the presheaf-to-sheaf maps. This is exactly the coefficient structure isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]: both send each local constant section $a$ to $a$ and glue on its open fibres, then extend by sheafification. Thus transport through this isomorphism in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] gives $j^*N=N|_U$ as left module sheaves. In particular its action on $W/U$ is the original $A_T(W)$-action transported to $A_U(W)$. No permutation of factors in $A$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 04IX, definition-localize-ringed-site; coefficient action and sheafification comparison from the cited nodes

proof.text: Use $(j_*G)(V)=G(V\times_TU)$ from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], with scalar action through $A_T(V)\to A_U(V\times_TU)$. The sheaf adjunction is explicit: a module map $\phi:N|_U\to G$ transposes to the map with component $\phi_{V\times_TU}\circ\operatorname{res}_{V\times_TU/V}:N(V)\to G(V\times_TU)$; conversely $\psi:N\to j_*G$ transposes on $W/U$ to $\psi_W$, using $W\times_TU\cong W$. The monomorphism clause (4) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] gives these identifications, and naturality at $V\times_TU\to V$ shows that the two formulas are inverse. Both are left-linear by the coefficient identification in step 2. For $\phi=\mathrm{id}_{N|_U}$ the first formula is $N(V)\to N(V\times_TU)$. It is also the unit of the specified inverse-image adjunction: in the colimit formula defining that adjunction, its coprojection indexed by $(V,\mathrm{id}_{V\times_TU})$ becomes restriction along $V\times_TU\to V$ under the initial-pair identification of step 1. Thus the adjunction, its action, and its unit have all been identified.

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; Tag 06UM, section-pullback, the colimit adjunction and unit

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] to the ring sheaf $A_T$ on the small site $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and its object $U$. This result is stated for sheaves of rings, including noncommutative ones (its recorded interface uses RingCat). Restriction preserves zero maps because every component of a restricted zero map is still zero. With the module identification of step 2 its conclusion is precisely that $j^*I$ is K-injective. Also [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] makes $j^*$ exact and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] therefore gives the termwise derived restriction with comparison $j^*Q_T=Q_Uj^*$.

For $S=T,U$, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] applies to $A_S$ without a commutativity assumption, and [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] supplies K-injective resolutions of every complex. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to $Q_Tj_*:K(\operatorname{Mod}(A_U))\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$. This functor is triangulated: termwise $j_*$ is additive by the section formula in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], hence takes a shifted complex to the shifted image and the cone $Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$ with its differential matrix to the identical cone matrix after $j_*$. Derived localization then takes these cone triangles to distinguished triangles. Consequently $Rj_*$ exists and its comparison $\beta_J:Q_Tj_*J\to Rj_*(Q_UJ)$ is an isomorphism for every K-injective $J$. Taking $J=j^*I$ gives the asserted representation.

source.place: Tags 070K and 070Y, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies and lemma-K-injective-defined; injectives.tex Tags 079P and 079Q

proof.text:
For a K-injective $J$ on $U$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applied to $j^*\dashv j_*$ and exactness of $j^*$ from [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] makes $j_*J$ K-injective. For every complex $M$ on $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] now gives the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U)}(Q_Uj^*M,Q_UJ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(U)}(j^*M,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(T)}(M,j_*J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T)}(Q_TM,Q_Tj_*J).$$
For the middle bijection use the formulas in step 3 degreewise. Naturality with respect to the two differentials carries the chain-map equation to the transposed chain-map equation. The same formulas applied to degree $-1$ maps carry $f-g=dh+hd$ to the identical equation for their transposes, since the formulas are additive; hence they give inverse maps on homotopy classes. Composing the last term with $\beta_J$ from step 5 gives the derived adjunction: all target objects have these K-injective representatives, and the bijections are natural in $M,J$. This is the adjunction induced from the specified sheaf adjunction and right-derived comparison, rather than an independently chosen adjunction.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors

proof.text: Set $M=I$ and $J=j^*I$ in step 6; the latter is K-injective by step 4. Under the Hom bijection the identity of $Q_Uj^*I$ is represented by $\mathrm{id}_{j^*I}$, whose sheaf-level transpose is $\eta_I:I\to j_*j^*I$ by step 3. Therefore its derived transpose, which defines the derived adjunction unit, is $\beta_{j^*I}\circ Q_T(\eta_I)$. Under the representation of step 5 (identifying the target via $\beta_{j^*I}$) this is exactly $Q_T(\eta_I)$. Its component in each degree over $V/T$ is the restriction $I^q(V)\to I^q(V\times_TU)$ computed in step 3. All identifications are natural, so this proves the specified unit, as well as the representation of the object.

title: Derived open direct image on a K-injective complex
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and $A$ a finite ring, not necessarily commutative. Use the small pro-etale sites and coefficient sheaves $A_S$ and left module categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], in compatible small skeletons and a common sheaf universe. The module inverse image $j^*$ with transported action [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] is identified with restriction to $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U=U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, including its coefficient action and adjunction unit. In particular $(j^*N)(W\to U)=N(W\to T)$, and the unit on an object $V\to T$ is restriction $N(V)\to N(V\times_TU)$, using the direct-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].

For every K-injective cochain complex $I$ of left $A_T$-module sheaves, the restricted complex $j^*I$ is K-injective. Here K-injective means that every chain map from an acyclic complex is homotopic to zero [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Let $Q_S$ denote derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $Rj_*$ be the total right derived functor of $j_*$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Then $Rj_*j^*(Q_TI)$ is represented by $Q_T(j_*j^*I)$. Under this representation and $Q_Uj^*I=j^*Q_TI$, the unit of the derived adjunction $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ at $Q_TI$ is $Q_T(I\to j_*j^*I)$, with the termwise restriction maps just specified.
